cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T3 narrows its claim in answer to T2 and turns T2's forecasting point back on friends.
cells.limitation: T4 sidesteps both prior arguments rather than answering either directly.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T6 adds the opposite test (build something your own); T7 and section E use it.
cells.limitation: T10 largely restates the T1 position, reframed as noise versus information.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: Borrowed comparison versus quiet wish is examined across T1, T2, T3 and T10.
cells.limitation: Nobody raises friendships drifting or belonging as friends change stage; family expectations also unraised.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T7 adopts the Experimenter's test as a way to settle its own comparison claim.
cells.limitation: The Forecaster never acknowledges T6's answer to its contamination objection in T5.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D: feeling behind and wanting these things are two separate signals.
cells.limitation: The comparison-versus-wish split was already framed in section A; progress is mostly in methods.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T2 states T1's scoreboard view fairly before testing it.
cells.limitation: T4 flattens T2's forecasting point into arguing about an inner truth.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T5 names the flaw in T4's trials (contaminated, one noisy signal); T6 answers with several trials.
cells.limitation: T7's worry that experiments become a new scoreboard is never answered.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T8 and T9 bases flag the regret test and timed pause as the speakers' own extensions.
cells.limitation: T1 applies Veblen's pecuniary emulation to marriage without flagging the extension (suspected stretch).

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T1 frames its claim as a bet; section D marks what stays disputed.
cells.limitation: T8 states that feelings of being behind loom then ease as a general fact.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T7 concedes the test is sharper and states what result would make it concede more.
cells.limitation: The Forecaster never revises after T6 answers its T5 objection.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: Section A separates the reported feeling from an unnamed wish versus crowd discomfort.
cells.limitation: What behind means to the user (belonging, timeline, family) is never opened as ambiguous.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T4 builds trials from the user's friends: helping one move, attending a wedding.
cells.limitation: Beyond friends' milestones, examples like trip or project in T6 are generic.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: No mind pushes homes or marriage; the user's uncertainty is treated as legitimate.
cells.limitation: The user's own priorities beyond these milestones are never surfaced or asked.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T9 names conditional constraints: a moving market, a partner wanting a family, an age window.
cells.limitation: Money and the cost of friendships changing stage go undiscussed.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on whether the feeling fades, persists, or a real constraint exists.
cells.limitation: Partner status, age and finances are folded into one branch, never asked directly.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: Borrowed comparison and quiet wish offered as alternatives; section D poses an answerable question.
cells.limitation: A third plausible motive, fear of losing closeness with friends, is not offered.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T2: not wanting it now isn't proof; T3: friends' certainty is also a guess.
cells.limitation: The assumption that life has a schedule one can be behind is not examined directly.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T6 points toward building something plainly yours as a counterweight.
cells.limitation: No turn names what the user values (security, freedom, belonging) or where those conflict.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T1 and T10 name crowd pressure; T9 names avoidance without pathologising.
cells.limitation: Fear of being left out as friends change, and family expectations, go unnamed.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: T9's passive versus dated waiting and T10's information versus noise are distinctions to accept or reject.
cells.limitation: Section D offers one reflective question; most distinctions stay as speaker claims.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: T8 adds waiting; section E lists own path, small step, and pause with check-in.
cells.limitation: What is actually being decided stays vague: handling the feeling or pursuing milestones.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: T9 states the cost of waiting; T7 the cost of experiments becoming a scoreboard.
cells.limitation: Section E's small reversible step toward a home or partner carries no stated cost.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: feeling fades when absorbed in own project favours own path; persists favours small step.
cells.limitation: T8's five years and section E's couple of months are not drawn from user facts.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section E names the consequential unknown: which pattern is true for the user.
cells.limitation: Minor unknowns are not separated from consequential ones such as a partner's timeline.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: Section E: a few low-cost trials, noting feelings afterward and in following days.
cells.limitation: The couple-of-months span is ungrounded; no first step is named concretely.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T1: falling behind on a scoreboard you never chose to play is still painful.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T3's your point refers unambiguously to T2; T10's you both to the other two minds.
cells.limitation: T7's that test could mean either of T6's two tests until the next sentence.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Ten turns, all within the word range, each making one move.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: Positions stay distinct: crowd noise (Status Observer), unreliable forecasts, test by action.
cells.limitation: All three minds share one crisp register and near-identical turn lengths across T1 to T10.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: No turn repeats an earlier one; sections D and E summarise distinct material.
cells.limitation: Section E partly restates section D's fading-feeling test.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T9: some doors do narrow, a partner who wants a family, an age window.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay abstract for most of the debate until T9.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T7 concedes the Experimenter's test is sharper than anything it offered, naming T6 as cause.
cells.limitation: The concession is conditional and partial; no mind fully changes position.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: T10's dry Status Observer: the ache as weather of a crowd at a different stage.
cells.limitation: Forecaster and Experimenter sound alike in register; personality rests mostly on stance.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T7: an experiment can become a new scoreboard, with hobbies as medals.
cells.limitation: The Forecaster's turns T2, T5, T8 carry no comparable image.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: T9 to T10 shift from method to an unresolved disagreement about the ache.
cells.limitation: Uniform turn length and steady measured intensity across T1 to T10 flatten rhythm.

strengths: T5 to T7: the contamination objection is answered by T6's several trials and opposite test, which T7 then adopts.
Section E gives observable conditions (does the feeling fade when absorbed in your own project) tied to options.
T9's distinction between passive waiting and waiting with a check-back date sharpens T8's waiting option.
weaknesses: No mind asks what the user values most, so the values cell (C4.3) stays thin.
Nobody raises friendships changing as friends marry and buy homes, a likely source of feeling behind.
All three minds share one register and near-identical turn lengths, flattening voice and rhythm.

symptoms.observed: No turn names the user's values or where they conflict; focus stays on testing desire.
symptoms.evidence: build something that is plainly yours, a trip, a project

symptoms.observed: Friends moving to a new stage is read only as a scoreboard, never as possible loss of closeness.
symptoms.evidence: When everyone around you buys homes and weddings, those become the scoreboard.

symptoms.observed: Partner, age and finances appear as hypotheticals but are never asked as questions.
symptoms.evidence: a partner who wants a family, an age window

symptoms.observed: Three minds share one crisp register and near-identical turn lengths.
symptoms.evidence: One trial is a noisy signal, and I'd distrust my own mood

symptoms.observed: Time frames proposed (five years, a season, a couple of months) are not drawn from user facts.
symptoms.evidence: ask what you'd regret in five years.

findings.description: Attributions to Veblen, Gilbert and Ibarra are general and plausible; no source evidence attached to confirm them.
Veblen's emulation concerns pecuniary display; extending it to marriage and home timing is a stretch not flagged as the speaker's extension.
Claim that feelings of being behind tend to ease is stated as general fact, an extrapolation from adaptation research.

rubric_fit_notes: The user gave very little context, so C3 cells reward conditional branching more than use of detail; ratings there reflect what could be done with a two-sentence situation. The decision framing fits loosely since the user named a feeling, not a choice.
raw.question_type_note: Read as a decision (self_reflection) question: cells were read as written, with the decision taken as how to treat the feeling and whether to move toward these milestones.
